fit: historical firsthand ginger report during gout attacks
assessment: The Stenhouse letter describes less pain during attacks and prolonged post-attack weakness after regular ginger use. The dose form, diagnosis and other exposures are unresolved. The later bath experiment is separate.

fit: reported short-term worsening and later relief after mixed intake
assessment: Harrison described initial abdominal pain worsening then relief after powdered ginger with sago and brandy. He reported bedtime opium after the relief. A self-observed course in one episode cannot separate natural fluctuation or any one ingredient.

fit: historical report of ginger infusion practice for rheumatic pain
assessment: The editorial reports worsening followed by later relief and attributes the practice to unnamed French surgeons. The underlying patients and original witness are unverified, and the root processing is unclear.

fit: common parsley in historical discussion of fits
assessment: Pages 557–558 identify garden parsley and relay historical concern about aggravated fits. Individual exposure and measured outcome are absent. A fit is a distinct outcome from Parkinson muscle rigidity.

fit: whole formula placebo comparison with regional transit and stool diaries
assessment: Sixty healthy participants were randomized. One active arm favored ascending-colon emptying, while gastric emptying, 24-hour colonic transit and stool outcomes were inconclusive. W1413 and NCT00871325 are members of the same family. No grated ginger contrast exists.

fit: two active formula doses and chronic constipation bowel diary
assessment: Twenty-two participants continued sennoside through active before–after phases. Stool frequency was inconclusive and neither dose group isolated ginger. T1829 supplies the same study comparison.

fit: constipation-associated pain in a whole formula add-on comparison
assessment: Table 4 shows VAS median 32 to 7 over six weeks in the higher-dose group (within-group p=.02) and 20 to 13 in the lower-dose group (p=.12). This is no randomized comparison with a group receiving sennoside alone, and the study supplies no separate ginger effect.

fit: single-arm planned symptom study and tentative publication relation
assessment: The registry describes one nonrandomized group and estimated n=60 with no posted results. The overlapping site and phases give a linkage lead, while the published two-dose cohort reports n=22. Evidence from the publication is assessed under its source key.
